entries.title: Laptop won't power on / no display
steps: Disconnect the charger and remove any USB devices, then hold the power button down for 30 seconds to drain residual (flea) power.
Reconnect the original Dell charger and confirm the charging LED lights up — a dead or wrong-wattage adapter is the most common cause.
Press the power button once and watch for keyboard backlight or fan noise; if you see activity but no image, connect an external monitor to rule out the display.
If there is still no power or no display, the unit likely needs on-site hardware service.

entries.title: Laptop overheating / shutting down / loud fan
steps: Place the laptop on a hard flat surface so the bottom intake vents aren't blocked, and make sure the side/rear exhaust vents are clear.
Use compressed air to clear dust from the vents, then check that the fan spins up under load.
Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) and end any single process pinned near 100% CPU; restart afterward to clear stuck processes.
If it still overheats or shuts down on its own, the cooling fan or thermal paste likely needs on-site service.
